1. VIEW THE MEETING LIVE ONLINE AT: https://youtube.com/@SouthGateCA90280
Please allow up to 24 hours after the meeting for the archive to be available.
2. PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING by emailing the City Clerk at:
yglaze@sogate.org no later than 4:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please write
"Public Comment" in the subject line.
3. ATTEND THE MEETING IN PERSON
*The disruption in service of any alternative method does not prelude the City Council
or other legislative
body from taking further action and moving forward on the agenda.

Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Call to Order/Roll Call With Invocation & Pledge
CALL TO ORDER:  Gil Hurtado, Mayor

INVOCATION:  Pastor Nick Garife, Gateway Assembly

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

ROLL CALL:  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

Meeting Compensation Disclosure
Pursuant to Government Code Section 54952.3: Disclosure of compensation for meeting
attendance by City Council Members is $790 monthly regardless of the amount of meetings.

Public Hearings - None
Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment

  2
 due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items

Agenda Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including
Ordinances, Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent
Calendar, individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion
of these items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific
items be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members
of the public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three
(3) minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after

  7
 the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

PURPOSE:  To consider adopting Ordinance No. 2024-04-CC authoiizing an amendment to tlie

FISCAL IMPACT:  The estimated savings from implementing  the cost sliaring program  for

NOTICING REQUIREMENTS:  A public hearing notice was duly publislied  in the South  Gate
Press, a newspaper of general circulation on Thursday, October 10, 2024.

ANALYSIS:  At the regular City Council meeting of October 22, 2024, the City Council heard
the staff report, took public coinment, and voted 5-0 to waive the reading in full and introduce the
attached Ordinance authorizing an amendment to the contract with CalPERS to implement a cost
sharing prograt'n between the City and the Division Managers' Association ("DMA")  employees,

("POA") employees.

  1

  9
 Califotania retirement law allows for two types of cost sliaring wliere employees pay a poition  of
tlhe employer contribution to CalPERS. The first type of cost sliaring is by CalPERS contract
atnendment under Goverru'nent Code ("GC") e)20516(a-e). In order for cost sliaring to be effective
under that method, CalPERS must first approve a contract amendment with the City. Tliis fon'n of
cost sharing is generally more favorable for employees, as tlie additional employee contiibutions
are considered by CalPERS to be "non'nal member contiibutions"  and are treated as pre-tax
contributions. As such, this is the cost-sharing metliod the City is proposing.

Tlie alternative method is cost sharing under GC Eg20516(f). That methodology is between tlie
City and its etnployees only, without a CalPERS contract amendment. Under GC Fg20516(f), the
additional employee contiibutions effectively subsidize tlie City's CalPERS contributions and are
considered after-tax contributions.

BACKGROUND:  The City's current contract with CalPERS provides that all employees  pay the
full employee share toward their retirement benefit. That contribution percentage differs based on
whether they are "Classic"  unit members or "PEPRA"  unit members. Duiing tl'ie most recent
contract negotiations between the City and the Executives, they agreed that they would participate
in a cost sharing program. The South Gate Police Management Association ("SGPMA")  was the
first labor group to participate in the cost sharing program by having all their "Classic"  unit
members contribute 2% of tlieir salary toward the City's share of their retirement benefits
begiru'iing in FY 2022-23. The final ordinance amending the CalPERS contract for the cost sharing
program with SGPMA was approved by the City Council at its February 14, 2023, meeting by
adopting Ordinance  No. 2023-01-CC.

The other employee associations, the Miscellaneous  Employees Association  ("MEA"),  the
Professional Mid-Management  Association ("PMMA"),  the Division Management Association
("DMA"),  and the Police Officers' Association ("POA"), followed with members agreeing to
participate in the cost sharing program by contributing 1% of their salary toward the City's share
of tlieir retirement benefits beginning in FY 2023-24. Tl'ie final ordinance amending the CalPERS
contract for the cost sharing program with MEA, PMMA, DMA, and POA was approved by tlie
City Council at its June 13, 2023, meeting. Tl'ie cost sharing program for eacli of these labor groups
is pursuant to California Govetnrnent Code 20516(a) and was effective in July 2023.

Staff began working with CalPERS to amend the City's contract to implement this change affecting
the employees of DMA, PMA, and POS in March 2024 and received approval and the necessary
infon'nation to move forward on July 17, 2024. Tlie cost sharing program  for tlie employees  of
DMA, PMA, and POA is pursuant to Califomia Governi'nent Code § 20516(a) and will be effective
on the payroll pay period beginning on December 15, 2024.

In order to proceed with amending the City's contract with CalPERS for cost sharing, CalPERS
requires a Resolution of Intention, an election of employees agreeing to the contract change, and
adoption of an ordinance amending the City's contract witli CalPERS. At its August 13, 2024,
meeting, City Council adopted Resolution No. 2024-59-CC declaring its intent to amend the
contract with CalPERS to implement a cost sharing program.  Furtliennore, the members of PMA
and POA conducted a secret ballot election with a majority of the members voted in favor of the
proposed cost sharing program, which was ceitified by tlie City Clerk on September 3, 2024. The
final step to amend the contract is to adopt an ordinance authorizing an amendment to the contract

N0. 539-PRK

PURPOSE:  To adopt a resolution  to teri'ninate  the Declaration  of Emergency  for the Urban
Orchard Project.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider adopting a Resolution  to
ten'ninate the Declaration of Emergency for the Urban Orchard, City Project No. 539-PRK.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The Urban  Orchard  Project
("Project")  has received a total of $30.5 million  in grant and other funds for design, construction,
operations,  and maintenance

ANALYSIS:  Construction  of the Project  was scheduled  to be completed  in early  2023.  On
December  29, 2022, however,  Los Angeles  County  Department  of Health  Solid Waste Division
("County")  issued  a Corrective  Action  Order  ("Order")  which  required  the City  to stop all
construction  activities  until  such a time  as a Post Closure  Land Use Plan ("PCLUP")  for the
Project  site was approved  by the County.  Construction  was approximately  80% complete,  thus
the Project  was in a concerning  state. On February  6, 2023,  the City  Council  responded  by
adopting  a Resolution  to declare  an emergency  and authorized  the repair,  replacement  and/or
maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related to tlie Project.  This was needed to expeditiously
address maintenance  and safety  issues on the Project  site, as well  as to procure  engineering
services to secure a PCLUP  and County  approval.  On September  27, 2024, the County  approved
the PCLUP  thus construction  may  now  resume.  The declaration  of emergency  may  now  be
terminated. With the issuance of the PCLUP,  the project  site has been deemed safe for public  use
as a municipal park.

  ANALYSIS:  The City's  sanitary  sewer  system  is equipped  with  a SmartCover  System  that is
  remotely  managed  by Hadronex.  It monitor  flow  levels  on a continuous  basis  at 30 critical
  locations  to minimize  the potential  for  Sanitary  Sewer  Overflows  ("SSOs").  When  activated,
  Hadronex  receives  alarnns from  the monitoring  devices  after  which  they  alert the Public  Works
  Department  to active  emergency  response  services.

 The  SmartCover  System  was  manufactured  by  Hadronex.  They  are the  only  vendor  in  the
industry  able to monitor  and operate  it. They  are also the only  vendor  able to communicate
remotely  with  the system.  The  City's  current  agreement  with  Hadronex  expires  December  31,
2024.  A new agreement  is recoininended  to be awarded  to Hadronex  on a sole source basis.  The
South  Gate Municipal  Code  Section  1.54.510  allows  sole sourcing  of contracts.  Specifically,
Section  1.54.510  Exemptions  from  Fonnal  and Informal  Bidding  Procedures,  provides  criteria
under  which  sole-source  can be  considered.  The  proposed  services  with  Hadronex  fits  the
criteria.

The proposed  Agreement  includes  work  to expend  the monitoring  system  to incorporate  two new
manhole  locations.  These manholes  were selected  due to the number  of stoppages  that have been
reported  by area residents  and services  by City  maintenance  crews.  With  these additions,  flows
will  be monitored  at these locations  continuously  to prevent  880.

The proposed  Agreement  is in the amount  of $184,249.  Year  one service  is proposed  in the
amount  of $65,771,  which  includes  $12,431  to install  a monitoring  system  at two  additional
manholes  and $53,340  for monitoring  and operations  of the SmartCover  system.

BACKGROUND:  The City's  sewer system  contains  more than 120 miles  of sewer pipeline  and
over  2,400  manholes.  More  than  five  million  gallons  of sewage  is transported  by the  sewer
system  daily,  and monitoring  flow  levels  on a continuous  basis is essential  to minimizing  SSOs.

The sewer system  is equipped  with  a SmartCover  System  which  monitor's  sewage  flow  levels  at
sewer  manholes  on  a continuous  basis.  The  SmartCover  System  is hardware  and  software
technology  that provides  real-time  notification  when  sewer  flows  are unusually  high.  Currently,
flows  are monitored  at 30 priority  and  strategic  manhole  locations.  The  system  has  been
instrumental  in  preventing  SSOs.  During  the past  three  years,  no  SSOs  have  occurred  and
approximately  110 were prevented.

Hadronex  currently  maintains  and operates  the SmartCover  System  under  Contract  No.  2021-
140-AC.  It provides  for three years  of service  from  January  1, 2022,  to December  31, 2024.  A
new agreement  is needed  to continue  services.

The  following  are highlights  of  the  proposed  Agreement:  (a)  installation,  monitoring  and
warranty  for two  new  locations,  (b) a three-year  term,  from  January  1, 2025,  to December  31,
2027,  (c) monitoring  and  operation  of  the  SmartCover  System,  and  (d)  maintenance  which
includes  replacement  parts,  communications  network  access,  web-site  service,  software
upgrades,  technical  support,  field  service,  and a one-year  warranty.

Monitoring  and operation  of the  SmartCover  System  includes  wireless  communications  with
City  staff,  technical  telephone  support,  alari'n processing,  website  access and maintenance,  after
hours technical  support,  standard  reports,  custom  reports,  graphic  display,  management  tools  and
software  upgrades.

CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  NOVEMBER  12, 2024

CALL  TO ORDER  Gil Hurtado,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to order  at
  6:48 p.m.

INVOCATION  Pastor Nick  Garife,  Gateway  Assembly

PLEDGE  OFALLEGIANCE  Nellie  Ruiz,  Deputy  Director  of Human  Resources

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor  Gil Hurtado,  Vice Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Council  Member  Maria  del
  Pilar Avalos,  Council  Member  Joshua Barron  and Council  Member  Al
  Rios;  City  Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager  Rob Houston,  City
  Attorney  Raul F. Salinas

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  - NON-AGENDA

ITEMS  Mario  Dominguez,  Resident  is upset at the result  of the recent  elections.

  Ruben  Pichardo,  Resident  is reporting  issues regarding  employee  Johanna
  making  up violation  codes to harass me since August  1, 2024.  Requesting
  assistance  to correct  this issue.

  Armando  Velasquez,  Kiwanis  announces  the Clean-up  and brunch  event at
  CasaAbuelita.  Bingo  Lottery  Night.  Food and Gift  Card Drive.

  Armando  Velasquez,  Resident  is not happy  that this year's  election  process
  did not include  Q&A's,  and independent  interviews.

  Ana,  Chamber  of Commerce  announces  future  events  for November  and
  December.

  Council  MemberAvalos  asked if parking  will  be allowed  on the Northside
  of SouthernAvenue  during  the Christmas  Parade.

  Darren  Arakawa,  Police  Chief  states that parking  will  not be allowed
  during  the parade.

EMAILS:  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk  explains  that emails  that received  to be read at
  council  meetings  are summarized.  If anyone  is interested  in having  their
  full  comments  heard  are welcomed  to attend  city council  meetings  in
  person.
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF NOVEMBER  12, 2024

  Amy  Lu, Leeland  Weave  Library  shares upcoming  events  at our local
EMAILS:
  libraries.

  Victor,  Resident  expresses  issues with  City  Clerk  actions  within  this recent

  election  process.

  Joseph Velasco  requests  an expedited  permit  review  process  for the

  Dominoes  expansion.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS

FROMCITYOFFICIALS  ArturoCervantes,DirectorofPublicWorksprovidesaCIPProject
  construction,  renovation  and resurfacing  updates.

  Steve Costley,  Director  of Parks & Recreation  thanks  residents  and

  community  for their  attendance  during  Halloween  Night  & Special
  Olympics  events.

  Meredith  Elguira,  Director  of Community  Development  responds  to Mr.

  Pichardo's  comments.  Currently,  looking  into his allegations.  Also,
  looking  into expediting  the process  for the Dominoe's  expansion.

  Wendy  O'Kelly,  Director  ofAdministrative  Services  provides  update  that

  staff is currently  working  on the Annual  Comprehensive  Financial  Report.

  Nelly  Cobos,  Deputy  Director  of Human  Resources  urges the public  to go

  to our city's  website  for job opportunities.

  Darren  Arakawa,  Police  Chief  thanks  community  and council  for their
  attendance  at the Family  Day at the Park. Received  great feedback.

  Rob Houston,  City  Manager  was able to participate  in the Halloween,
  Veterans  Day, and Family  Day at the Park events  and appreciates  the
  community  participation.

  Raul F. Salinas,  City Attorney  has nothing  to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer  has nothing  to report.

  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk  has nothing  to report.

  Council  Member  Avalos  thanks  the community  for their  participation  in

  this year's  elections.  Attended  Family  Day at the Park. Appreciated  the

  hard work  of the Police  Dept. during  the Trunk  or Treat event.

  Page 2 of 7
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF NOVEMBER  12, 2024

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS
FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Council  Member  Rios congratulations  council  members  for this election
  and those who participated.  Attended  Family  Day at the Park and enjoyed
  seeing  all who attended.  Thank  you, Veterans  and their families.

  Would  like to ask the Chief  about the new administration  and worries
  regarding  our immigrant  community.

  Darren  Arakawa,  Chief  of Police  states that we do not enforce  immigration
  laws. Not our jurisdiction.  We do not ask immigration  status. We will
  arrest those that commit  crimes  in our  cornrnunity.

  Council  Member  Barron  honored  to attend the Veteran's  Day event.
  Attended  Family  Day at the Park. Thank  you to the organizations  that
  participated  in our events.  Looking  forward  to Breakfast  with  Santa.

  Vice Mayor  Davila  announces  the Power  Gateway  $8,000  rebate meetings
  November  16, 2024,  and November  19, 2024. Thank  you to Steve Costley
  and his staff for amazing  events.  Thank  you to detective  Sarah Medrano
  and Tony Mendez  on the Fentanyl  Presentation  for South  Gate Middle
  School  parents.

  Mayor  Gil Hurtado  attended  meeting  with  elected  officials  regarding
  issues with  broadband.

  Thank  you to our South  Gate employees  for making  sure our events  are
  safe for our community.

  Responds  to Mr. Pichardo's  comments.  I try my best to bring  back
  anyone's  issues to our staff. We strive  to do everything  we can to assist our
  cornrnunity.

  Elections  are stressful  but we offer  our commitment  to our community.  We
  might  have differences,  but we will  respect  the vote of the people.
